sources.note: HHMI Janelia Research Campus's own application-details page for the Joint Graduate Program: entry requirements, the requirement to name one to four Janelia Group Leaders, the December 3 deadline, and the April 15 notification date.

HHMI Janelia's programme overview page: states the programme is a fully-funded collaborative PhD programme in partnership with the Solomon Snyder Department of Neuroscience at The Johns Hopkins University; degrees are granted by Johns Hopkins.

HHMI Janelia's Additional Information page: visa sponsorship, additional degree requirements, TOEFL/IELTS requirements with US/UK degree waiver, and the financial support and benefits package for graduate scholars.

awarding_body.detail: The pages are on janelia.org, HHMI Janelia Research Campus's own site (footer links to hhmi.org). The programme is run by HHMI Janelia in partnership with the Solomon Snyder Department of Neuroscience at Johns Hopkins University, which sits within JHU's School of Medicine - matching the record's 'HHMI Janelia Research Campus, in collaboration with Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine'. Degrees are granted by Johns Hopkins.
awarding_body.quote: The Janelia Joint Graduate Program is a fully-funded, collaborative PhD program for independent, committed graduate scholars in partnership with the Solomon Snyder Department of Neuroscience at The Johns Hopkins University.

deadline.detail: The page states 'December 3' with no year, exactly as the record's deadline_label notes ('annual; the official page states no year'). Students apply in the fall for the following year's intake, so the cycle open today (12 October 2026) closes December 3, 2026 - a future deadline, not a past one. The record's deadline_date of 2026-12-03 is therefore the correct currently-open cycle date. The page also states decisions are communicated by April 15.
deadline.quote: The deadline for submission of completed applications, including letters of recommendation is December 3.

eligibility.detail: All four distinct eligibility claims in the record were confirmed: (1) B.S. or B.A. holders - the page says applicants 'should have a B.S. or B.A.' (record says 'must hold'; the difference is the page's softer wording, not a different requirement); (2) applying directly to the Johns Hopkins neuroscience programme, with no separate Janelia application; (3) naming one to four Janelia Group Leaders as thesis-research hosts; (4) TOEFL or IELTS required for students from non-English-speaking countries. The Additional Information page adds that the TOEFL requirement can be waived for applicants who completed a degree in the U.S. or U.K. - a supplementary detail, not a contradiction.
eligibility.quote: TOEFL or IELTS scores are required for students from non-English-speaking countries.

funding.detail: The programme overview page describes the programme as fully funded, and the Additional Information page states scholars are fully supported financially by their labs and the graduate program, listing a stipend (JHU-equivalent in year one, a Janelia Graduate Scholar Stipend at Janelia), health insurance and other benefits, payment of all programmatic travel costs, conference travel, and free housing at Janelia during lab rotations. This is full financial support, not tuition-only. One caveat: the stipend/benefits bullet list is labelled 'for the 2023/2024 Academic Year', so the specific amounts are dated even though the fully-funded status is stated without a year on the programme page.
funding.quote: Graduate scholars are fully supported financially by their labs & the graduate program during their research.

degree_levels.detail: The programme is a PhD (doctoral) programme only: the overview page calls it a 'collaborative PhD program', the application page describes students conducting 'their Ph.D. research at Janelia', and the Additional Information page states degrees are granted by Johns Hopkins (the page's text contains a typographical doubling, 'the The Johns Hopkins University', quoted verbatim). No bachelor's or master's degree is offered through this programme, matching the record's 'PhD'.
degree_levels.quote: Degrees are granted by the The Johns Hopkins University. [sic]

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: The deadline for submission of completed applications, including letters of recommendation is December 3. (The official page states no year; the cycle open on 12 October 2026 closes December 3, 2026. All candidates are notified of the Admission Committee's decision by April 15.)
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Checked live on 2026-10-12 against three pages on janelia.org (Application Details, programme overview, Additional Information); all are the awarding body's own site and all three loaded successfully. The deadline is published as 'December 3' with no year - each re-check should confirm which cycle is open and attach the correct year. The application itself is submitted to the Johns Hopkins Neuroscience programme (neuroscience.jhu.edu/graduate/apply); Janelia requires no separate application. The stipend and benefits list on the Additional Information page is dated '2023/2024 Academic Year' while the programme overview states 'fully-funded' without a year, so funding wording should be re-checked when a newer amount is published. The record's wording 'must hold a B.S. or B.A.' softens the page's 'should have a B.S. or B.A.' - substantively the same requirement.
